biography.plain_text: Allen Stanford is an American former financier convicted of orchestrating a vast investment fraud through Stanford International Bank. He built an offshore banking business that sold certificates of deposit while diverting customers’ funds into his own ventures. In 2012, a Houston federal court sentenced him to 110 years in prison.

long_biography.plain_text:
American former financier Allen Stanford bought the Waco fitness club where he had worked as a student. He expanded it into a Texas chain, selling membership contracts to raise cash. Expansion during the oil downturn ended in business failure and personal bankruptcy, preceding his move into Caribbean banking.

Stanford created a regional Twenty20 cricket tournament and recruited former West Indies players to its governing board. He also negotiated with England’s cricket authorities about further competitions. The venture was among the personal businesses financed with misappropriated bank deposits, rather than the investment profits presented to customers.
